references.text: The same law concerning kidnapping and human trafficking is found in Exodus, where the death penalty is also prescribed for anyone who steals a person
Laws regarding taking care of another's property and returning what is found, demonstrating concern for fellow humans' belongings
The prohibition against stealing is part of the fundamental ethical laws that protect human dignity
The same formulation about purging evil from among the people is used here, showing the seriousness of the crime
The same expression about purging evil from society is used in connection with other serious crimes
Repetition of the principle of purging evil from among the people in connection with false witnesses
Joseph was sold by his brothers to the Midianites, an example of human trafficking among Israelites
Joseph himself describes that he was stolen from the land of the Hebrews, showing his understanding that he was a victim of kidnapping
Paul mentions slave traders among those who act against sound doctrine, showing that this law remained relevant
Human trafficking ('human souls') is mentioned as part of Babylon's sinful trade that is condemned
